links.title: Sankai Juku
links.note: Sankai Juku (山海塾) — Japanese butoh company co-founded in 1975 by Amagatsu Ushio, who directs, choreographs and still dances. The name means “sea and mountain lodgings”. All-male, shaved heads, bodies whitened with powder; long meditative passages of near-stillness, ritual patterns that fracture into sharp disjointed sequences, spare sets and very delicate lighting. Amagatsu: “butoh is a dialogue with the gravity” — the other dance forms revel in escaping it. Worth knowing before watching: the signature upside-down motif from “Sholiba”, dancers hung from the fronts of buildings, is the one that killed founding member Yoshiyuki Takada in Seattle on 10 Sep 1985 when his rope gave way — the rigging had been tested with sandbags, but only one rope. “Kinkan Shonen” had a live peacock. Saved 4 Nov 2026 at M's request, not yet watched.

links.title: Ugly milkshake duck
links.note: Rafe Meager, The Universal and the Vacuous Events, 30 Oct 2026 — about 7,000 words, three years in the writing. Read 1 Nov: M's verdict was “fantastic”. Turns the milkshake-duck frame (the thing you love turns out rotten) on X and its owner, then on the author herself: twenty years of living on text social media. Two threads worth the time: a defence of hatred — not as a defect in the hater, but as a functional emotion, with the new-age Jungian reading blamed for the confusion — and a quoted DM that maps five escalating positions, from “I want this, you seem not to, I apologise for my mistake” through “but I know you do” to “there is no you”, which is the ramp to abuse. Ends on politics and the impossibility of separating public existence from it.

links.title: Brick
links.note: A small NFC puck you tap on your phone to block the apps that eat the day — one tap to brick it, one tap to unblock. Physical, so it can't be talked out of like a settings screen can; there are family and organisation versions. Direct-to-consumer Shopify store, so read the marketing with a pinch of salt. Saved 31 Oct 2026 at M's request, still unread.

links.title: How to be more ambitious: a tutorial for humans with models
links.note: Felix Rieseberg (works on Claude) splits ambition into Speed, Altitude, Depth and Range. Altitude: ask for the outcome, not the task — “keep our apps crash-free”, not “fix this crash”; a good sign it applies is when you would otherwise hold meetings about the work. Depth: insist on the instruments real experts use (databases and statistical models, not markdown tables), set an unreasonable target and insist it is reasonable, and make the model adversarially re-derive what you believe from raw data. Not model-specific.

links.title: LibrePaper
links.note: Collaborative writing in HTML, LaTeX, Typst, Markdown, Quarto and Calepin: real-time cursors, threaded comments, tracked changes, version history. MIT and self-hostable, and it brings your own AI agent (Claude Code, Codex, opencode) into the document rather than selling you one. Free tier is limited by storage.

links.title: Bead Me Up, Scotty
links.note: Human-facing viewer and editor for Beads — Steve Yegge's Dolt-backed graph issue tracker built for AI agents. Saved 26 Oct 2026, still unread.
